reasons.reader_question: Kiran's final line interrupts a confession in progress; the reader needs Rohan's response to the truth Meera paid two fingers to hide.
reasons.change: Captive to free and armed: the seal is recovered, Varun is exposed through ledger and witness, and Asha switches sides.
reasons.romance_movement: She hands him her load for the first time. The reason is new: the rope makes 'I've got it' a lie now.
reasons.shown_chemistry: Chemistry shows in action: the cord held taut without touch, him retying the double hitch, the swallowed 'May I', the sattu joke.
reasons.character_logic: Meera trades well, but stitching a brand-new button under thread sewn 'ten winters back' breaks logic. Asha's silencing look is under-motivated.
reasons.stakes_and_cost: Dead fingers come off on a deadline after the Fair, and Kiran's confession puts Rohan's oath and his law at risk.
reasons.prose: Concrete and readable, but there are told beats ('Her whole face changed'), stacked 'did not' negations, and cold stone pulled from steaming tea.
reasons.continuity: Nimmi's 'a day after, no more' conflicts with F260 (she amputates two days after the Fair). The ten-winter stitching conflicts with F052's new button.

fixes: At 'She had sewn them herself, ten winters back': the button is new this winter (F052), so this is a logic break. Change it to say she has re-stitched the spine after every drop for ten winters, and sewed this button in the night after the chapter 1 drop. Keep the habit; fix the date.

At 'After the Fair. A day after, no more.': this conflicts with F260, where Nimmi amputates two days after the Fair. Change it to 'Two days after, no more,' and keep the threat that the rot reaches the wrist. Also update 'Two fingers. A day.' to 'Two days.'

At 'Asha's eyes went to it. Her whole face changed.': this is narrated reaction. Replace it with an action, such as her knife hand going still or her thumb rubbing the pewter button on her own cuff, before she speaks. Separately, at 'and then on cold stone', make the stone hot from the tea, so the reader isn't left with cold stone pulled from steaming water.
reader_question: What will Rohan do when Kiran tells him he was the smuggler on Dilan's rope?
new_facts_assessment: Crate marks are useful and consistent: the scored bell echoes the regent's store mark (F217). The spine-stitching fact conflicts with F052, since the button arrived new this winter. The 'May I' fact stretches the ch27 promise, which covered only that rope, into all questions. It is acceptable as scrupulousness but should be stated as her reading.
